title: Obsession Crosses $500 Million Worldwide, Enters All-Time Top 5 Horror Films
excerpt: Curry Barker's micro-budget horror sensation surpasses The Conjuring: Last Rites to become the fifth-highest-grossing horror film in history, delivering a staggering 670x return on its $750,000 budget.
body:
• Obsession has crossed $501.5 million worldwide, surpassing The Conjuring: Last Rites ($499.2 million) to enter the all-time top 5 highest-grossing horror films.
  • The film, made on an estimated $750,000 budget by 26-year-old YouTuber-turned-director Curry Barker, has delivered one of the largest returns on investment in cinema history.
  • In India, Obsession collected ₹99.25 crore gross, narrowly missing the ₹100 crore milestone and finishing as the second-highest-grossing Hollywood horror film in the country.
  • Breakout star Inde Navarrette, who earned critical acclaim for her role as Nikki, has been cast in Marvel's new X-Men franchise.

A $750,000 Film Joins an Elite Club

Obsession has officially entered one of cinema's most exclusive clubs. Curry Barker's supernatural horror film has crossed the $500 million mark worldwide, making it only the fifth horror movie in history to reach that milestone.

With $501.5 million in global earnings as of this week, Obsession has overtaken The Conjuring: Last Rites ($499.2 million) for the fifth spot on the all-time horror box office list, according to Box Office Mojo. The film sits behind World War Z ($540 million), I Am Legend ($585.5 million), The Sixth Sense ($672.8 million), and Stephen King's It ($719.7 million), the genre's all-time champion.

What makes the achievement extraordinary is the scale of the return. Obsession was produced for an estimated $750,000—a microscopic sum by Hollywood standards—delivering roughly a 670x return on its production budget.

The Rise of a Gen Z Horror Phenomenon

Barker, a 26-year-old who got his start creating content on YouTube before making his feature debut with Milk & Serial in 2024, premiered Obsession at the 2025 Toronto International Film Festival. Focus Features acquired the film for around $14 million, and it opened theatrically in the United States on May 15, 2026.

The film became a viral sensation among younger audiences, holding the No. 2 spot at the domestic box office for a month straight and becoming Focus Features' highest-grossing release ever. It is currently the fifth-highest-grossing film of 2026 domestically with $262.8 million in North American earnings.

"This year has marked a turning point for the box office with Gen Z-driven horror movies setting records as existing franchises struggle."

— Polygon

Paired with Backrooms, another Gen Z-helmed horror success that has crossed $395 million globally, Obsession signals a clear appetite among younger moviegoers for original horror content over franchise sequels.

A Near-Century in India

Obsession's performance in India was equally remarkable. The film collected ₹99.25 crore gross during its theatrical run, narrowly missing the coveted ₹100 crore milestone. Its early OTT premiere is widely seen as the reason it fell short of the century mark.

The film remains the second-highest-grossing Hollywood horror film at the Indian box office, trailing only The Conjuring: Last Rites (₹100.50 crore gross). Its second week in India was 43% larger than its opening week—a rare feat for any film—driven by strong word-of-mouth among Indian audiences.

Breakout Stars and What's Next

The film centers on Bear (Michael Johnston), a music store employee who uses a supernatural "One Wish Willow" to make his crush Nikki (Inde Navarrette) fall in love with him, unleashing horrific consequences. The cast also includes Cooper Tomlinson, Megan Lawless, and Andy Richter.

Navarrette has emerged as the film's breakout star, earning critical acclaim and the 2026 Seattle International Film Festival's Best Performance award. She has since been cast in Marvel's new X-Men franchise, cementing her transition from indie horror to major studio productions.

With international markets still contributing earnings despite the film's availability on streaming platforms, Obsession's final worldwide tally could climb further. For now, it stands as a defining box office story of 2026—proof that audiences will flock to original content regardless of budget size.
